summary: One task: make flipped sleeves (offset < 0) ignore hit testing in CrateBox.vue while they stay drawn with the same transform and opacity, and add the AC5 unit test. The browser tester writes the real-input proof at test stage.

tasks.goal: Stop flipped sleeves catching pointer input, without changing how they are drawn, and pin the retained rendering with a named unit test.
tasks.description:
Defect (diagnosed from code, not yet reproduced): in apps/web/src/components/crate/CrateBox.vue, the rule `.crate > * { pointer-events: auto; }` from commit 57302be applies to every sleeve. A flipped sleeve has offset < 0 and pose transform 'translateZ(40px) rotateX(-55deg)', opacity 0, zIndex 101. Its tipped top edge comes forward of the front panel's translateZ(70px), so it takes clicks aimed at the panel, and onSleeveClick(offset, album) then calls flip.goTo(index.value + offset), which moves back. Up to two flipped sleeves exist, because visibleRange(index, count) starts at index - 2.

Fix in CrateBox.vue: add one entry to the existing :style object on div.sleeve: `pointerEvents: offset < 0 ? 'none' : undefined`. Use the inline style instead of a class because the object already holds the pose, inline beats `.crate > *` without a specificity argument, and it can be asserted in happy-dom, which does not apply scoped CSS. pointer-events inherits, so SleeveArt and .divider-tab inside a flipped sleeve are covered too (nothing in them sets pointer-events: auto). The value applies as soon as index changes, so a sleeve still animating out is also excluded. Extend the comment at the `.crate` rule, or add one beside the new style entry, saying why flipped sleeves are excluded: they are invisible but tipped in front of the panel.

Do not change: sleevePose, visibleRange or anything else in crateLayout.ts; onSleeveClick; useCrateFlip.ts; the .panel.front markup or its pointer events (pointer-events: none on the panel would let clicks reach the current sleeve and open the album, failing AC1). Do not remove flipped sleeves with v-if or display:none, and do not filter them out of `drawn`. Do not only add an offset < 0 guard in the click handler, because the invisible sleeve would still be the hit target. Keep the visible back-sleeve behaviour (offset > 0 flips forward) and offset 0 opening the record.

Unit test in apps/web/src/components/crate/CrateBox.test.ts: add a new `it` in the top-level describe with a clear name, e.g. 'keeps flipped sleeves drawn for the flip-out animation, without catching clicks'. Use the existing helper mountCrate(2); its fixture has three albums, so index 2 gives two flipped sleeves (offsets -2 and -1) plus the current one. Take `wrapper.findAll('.sleeve').filter((s) => !s.classes().includes('current'))`, assert length 2, and for each read `(s.element as HTMLElement).style` and assert transform === 'translateZ(40px) rotateX(-55deg)', opacity === '0' (adjust only the comparison form if happy-dom serialises it differently, not the meaning) and pointerEvents === 'none'. Also assert the `.sleeve.current` element has no inline 'none' for pointerEvents. The existing test 'flips to a record further back when you click its edge' must stay byte-for-byte unmodified.

Do not create or edit .shipyard/checks/browser.mjs; the browser tester owns it. AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC6 are verified at test stage and depend on this fix being the only behaviour change.

Conventions: Prettier (no semis, single quotes, width 100, trailing commas). Commit as e.g. fix(web): stop invisible flipped sleeves catching clicks. No merge or push.

Before handing back, from the repo root run: npm test --workspace apps/web, npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check. All must exit 0.
